summary_html: Case dismissed due to **unsubstantiated evidence** or court determination that allegations not proven. Federal oversight requires accurate recording of such closures for audit and funding compliance.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — defines data-collection standards for unfounded cases  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — requires tracking and reporting of unsubstantiated outcomes

primary_citations.citation_text: New York - N.Y. Soc. Serv. Law § 411 et seq. (Child Protective Services Act – reporting requirements)
New York - Family Court Act Article 10 (Abuse/Neglect juvenile proceedings)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Court held that Family Court Act article 10-A confers no independent grant of continuing jurisdiction, so once an article 10 neglect petition is dismissed for failure to prove neglect the court loses subject matter jurisdiction and may not conduct further permanency hearings.
key_cases.relevance: This is the leading New York authority on the jurisdictional consequences of dismissing an abuse or neglect petition.
key_cases.quote: the dismissal of a neglect petition terminates Family Court's jurisdiction

key_cases.court: Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of the State of New York, First Department
key_cases.holding: The First Department held that Family Court may grant a suspended judgment retroactively after a parent has completed the terms of a dispositional order, vacating the neglect finding and dismissing the petition where that serves the children's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: This is the published New York authority permitting vacatur of a neglect finding and dismissal after successful completion of services.
key_cases.quote: Family Court Act § 1051 (c) authorizes dismissal upon two separate and distinct grounds
